item.title: Monitoring a Self-Hosted LLM Stack: vLLM, Phoenix, and Grafana Measurements
item.description: Running a self-hosted LLM stack produces signals on several axes at once — serving health, per-tenant token consumption, response quality, and full request traces. Classic web monitoring does not capture most of them. Tokens, batching, KV cache pressure, queue dynamics, inter-token latency, and trace spans all need their own measurement. This post is a practical guide to monitoring a self-hosted LLM inference stack. It covers what to measure at each layer (vLLM serving, AI Gateway access, Phoenix tracing and evaluation), which PromQL queries turn raw metrics into dashboards, how KEDA autoscaling consumes the signals, and which SLOs and alerts belong on the platform. The examples assume two NVIDIA DGX Spark units running vLLM, but the metrics and queries apply to any vLLM-based stack.

item.title: How to Backup and Restore Prometheus
item.description: Backing up Prometheus is critical for preserving your monitoring history and metrics data. This updated guide for 2026 covers modern backup strategies using the Prometheus Admin API, Velero, and volume snapshots in Kubernetes environments with prometheus-operator.

item.title: Send pfSense Logs to Wazuh
item.description: Centralizing pfSense firewall logs in Wazuh SIEM provides critical security visibility and threat detection capabilities. This updated guide for 2026 covers pfSense 2.7.x/2.8.x and Wazuh 4.8+ with proper syslog formatting and decoder configuration.
